What that cannot show is whether `tests/gate.rs` would notice if a

injections.name: the-artifact-join-is-removed
injections.why: cargo never garbage-collects dep-info, so sweeping the target directory credits units that no longer exist; the credit is invisible on a cold runner and decisive on a warm machine, which is the worst kind of disagreement

injections.name: the-default-feature-resolve-is-dropped
injections.why: `--all-features` is what makes a file behind a feature visible and what makes a file behind `not(feature)` invisible; with only the first resolve the second class is reported as uncompiled while cargo compiles it on every push

injections.name: the-probe-stops-asking-for-every-target
injections.why: `cargo check` without `--all-targets` compiles neither examples nor test entry points, so the population shrinks to libraries and binaries and every `tests/*.rs` in the repository reads as uncompiled

injections.name: a-build-script-joins-by-a-name-cargo-does-not-write
injections.why: cargo reports `build/<unit>/build-script-build` and rustc wrote `build/<unit>/build_script_build-<hash>`; joined by filename alone no build script ever matches, and every package with one turns the gate into a refusal

injections.name: the-self-check-against-cargos-own-target-list-is-removed
injections.why: cargo naming a target whose root nothing was measured to read is two answers disagreeing; without the check the gate reports whatever the mismatched record happened to name, confidently and about another unit

injections.name: an-unreadable-file-swallows-the-finding-it-is
injections.why: whether anything compiles a file was already decided by two sets; letting the second question — what is inside it — cancel the first lets an unreadable file hide the defect it is

injections.name: source-that-does-not-parse-reports-no-tests
injections.why: an empty answer and an unknown one are the same list; reporting zero tests for a file syn could not read understates every finding it appears in

injections.name: the-population-stops-being-what-git-tracks
injections.why: a file git does not track is not this repository's and a CI checkout does not have it; walking the disk instead makes the verdict a fact about the machine the gate ran on

injections.name: a-tree-holding-no-rust-becomes-a-pass
injections.why: zero tracked files is the shape of a gate pointed at the wrong tree, and it prints exactly like a repository where every file compiles

injections.name: a-workspace-this-machine-cannot-compile-stops-being-exempt
injections.why: `studio` is checkable here and skipped on every hosted runner, so counting its files as uncompiled makes the verdict a fact about which machine ran the gate rather than about the repository

injections.name: an-exception-in-a-declined-workspace-is-judged-anyway
injections.why: R1108 — the other side of the same asymmetry, and it had no injection because a second call site appeared with the same three lines and left the one above matching twice, which made the WHOLE sweep refuse. An entry for a file in a workspace this machine declines is a question this run has no answer to: it cannot see the file compiled, so it must not call the entry live, and it cannot see it uncompiled either, so it must not call it dead. Judging it anyway makes the gate reject on the runner and pass here off the same table
